header.purpose: A traceable requirement -> implemented profile -> source/model entry point -> executed test stage -> proof/evidence -> remaining-boundary matrix for revision 0.3 as implemented at this checkpoint.
header.counts_are_run_metadata: Every count in this file is run metadata about executed gates, manifests and archived measurements. A count is NOT proof of specification coverage: passing test totals, CT mapping counts, contract module counts and audit unit totals say what was executed, not what was proved. Projection coverage is not safety coverage and unknowns stay in the denominator.
header.verdict_vocabulary: Safe only after all obligations discharge; Unsafe only for a validated reachable violation; everything else Unknown. A provisional Unsafe is never presented as an upstream defect. Raw Cycle 19 units remain unpromoted.
header.independence_rule: The four evidence classes are marked INDEPENDENTLY per requirement. Support in one class is never inferred from another: a proved Lean theorem is not source evidence, an executed native run is not a model proof, and a model regression is not an observation.

evidence_classes.source: evidence taken on real source - QCore source programs through the frontend/driver, or C translation units through the gateway importers
evidence_classes.model: evidence taken in the dependency-free Rust kernel or the trusted verification adapter, over supplied traces, programs or certificates
evidence_classes.observation: evidence from an executed run - native/C11 execution, a CLI probe, a configured audit or a process provider
evidence_classes.mechanized: Lean 4 definitions and theorems registered in an Audit*.lean file and checked by scripts/check_lean_audits.py

support_status_vocabulary.executed: a named gate in the standing per-change gate runs this evidence class at HEAD
support_status_vocabulary.recorded_not_gated: the evidence exists as an archived probe log or transcript; nothing in the standing gate re-runs it
support_status_vocabulary.declared_premise: this class is an explicitly named assumption carried on the certificate/report, not established here
support_status_vocabulary.absent: no evidence of this class exists for this requirement
support_status_vocabulary.not_applicable: this class cannot apply to the requirement as stated

requirements.remaining_boundary: Observation scope/module/bounds substitution rejects; native provenance is declared trusted evidence and whole-program/source-model refinement remains open. Identity is provenance, not attestation: the compiler executable, its environment and the filesystem are trusted. Individual headers are not enumerated - the dependency closure is bound by effect through preprocessed_source_sha256 under -E -P, so a header edit that leaves the token stream unchanged does not change the identity. The declared driver is recorded, never checked for equivalence. The pinned Cycle19 compatibility adapter keeps CSourceInput::HistoricalStdin and its silent choice among 28 units with two or four compile configurations (G01 SS5); its four archived artifacts were not re-measured. Syntax and typed-AST phases still read preprocessed text from standard input, which is why __builtin_FILE/__builtin_FILE_NAME reject rather than being answered. P01-F2 is open: qcorec plugins verify/enable accept schema-valid, digest-intact edits to non-digest manifest declarations. P02 is not an OS sandbox: no namespace, cgroup, seccomp or capability-drop mechanism; no filesystem or network confinement (P03); RLIMIT_NPROC is per-UID and must not be presented as a per-execution child quota; non-Linux refuses rather than partially enforcing; the enforced profile is never selected by default.

Eleven named blockers (O00-B01..B11) include an unmodeled constructor publication in tension with the declared owned result, an undeclared mk_list_add, an unenumerated CIO_RETRY/CIO_CORRUPTED caller exit, and two unresolved aliases plus one unresolved callback. The O04 recommendation is deliberately narrow - per-arm cleanup discharge on four early-return arms only - and needs C02-P, array-declarator admission, three borrowed callee declarations and per-exit disposition. Lifting the indirect-access gate there also unmasks a discarded owned result elsewhere and would move all four archived 185-unit artifacts.

ct_conformance.derivation_rule: a stage is 'executed' only where a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact (T00's rule). No row claims a stage its executed evidence does not carry; manifest_stages is retained beside stage_derived_status so the divergence stays visible rather than being resolved silently.
known_manifest_overstatements: O1 - No assertion targets a CFG artifact. The sequential resource CFG is provably NOT run: compile_task_source (crates/qcore-verification/src/driver.rs:1100-1212) never calls synthesize_semantics or check_whole_program, and returns reference_observation: None. The claim is defensible only under the unstated reading 'cfg' = the task IR's blocks/terminators, which is exercised transitively by check_task_module/emit_task_c11 but never independently checked.

O2 - Both reject at Q600 in qcore_core::task_execution::check_task_module -- the task ledger, which runs AFTER elaboration and after lower_source_tasks. The two-stage label makes a deep ledger rejection indistinguishable from a shallow Q013 name-resolution rejection. Verified: CT02 expects Q600 'not an initialized owned buffer', CT19 expects Q600 'ScopeBusy'.

O3 - The runners are Linux-gated: on a non-Linux host every run_native_* helper returns after unsupported_target() and prints 'unexecuted on this host'. reference_execution, cfg and native_backend then do not execute, yet the manifest field still reads 'executed'. The manifest `note` acknowledges the scoping in prose; the machine-readable field a summarizer consumes does not.

O4 - No workspace test compiles any CT fixture with -fsanitize. native_fault_run uses '-std=c11 -pthread -Wall -Wextra -Werror' only. The sanitizer evidence is a transcript pasted into the report (docs/reports/w6-*/README.md), re-run by no gate. The only sanitized C in the workspace (crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/c_emit.rs) runs a different, sequential corpus.

O5 - The link is narrative only. ct_corpus.rs:260-264 asserts expected.positive_control.is_some() == (case.id == "CT19"), so CT02 is structurally forbidden from carrying a control. Nothing in the harness ties CT02's rejection to CT01's acceptance; if CT01 were retired, CT02's claim would silently become false.

O6 - run_positive_control DOES execute a Linux-gated task reference execution on joined_sibling.qcore (root outcome 42, 2 children, both joined). That executed evidence is recorded nowhere in the manifest, and the case carries no evidence_target even though its control is Linux-gated. The control is never compiled or run natively.

O7 - acceptance.json carries NO per-CT rows at all -- only these two scalars. The scalar treats CT02 (source rejection, zero native runs) and CT16 (4 reference executions + 4 native runs) as one unit of coverage, and hides that 0 of 11 cases have proof evidence and 0 of 11 have gated sanitized-native evidence. R02 and R04 cite the w6-* reports and state their boundaries accurately in prose; the defect is that the consumable numbers are binary.

O8 - Correct and not an overclaim -- recorded here because it is the largest uniform gap. No Lean theorem is bound to any CT fixture; the only CT string in proof/ is a comment at proof/QCore/TaskExecution.lean:539 naming CT13. The task theorems constrain the Lean model, and source/native refinement is an explicit premise in every w6 report.

O9 - Both fixtures' completion_before_join.h is a 66-byte one-line #include of compiler/tests/fixtures/task_worker_allocations/completion_before_join.h. The inventory assertion covers the stub, not the adapter that actually forces worker completion before creation returns. The shared adapter is outside the CT fixture tree and outside the inventory check.

The pin gate refused to run in this environment, so nothing was adjusted to fit.
named_followups.invariants: hard invariants 3 (parity before deletion) and 5 (pinned expectations are intentional): regenerate, diff, archive the diff under docs/reports/ and re-pin deliberately.

named_followups.title: Complete the source function enumeration (macro-expanded and K&R definitions)
named_followups.why: such definitions carry no obligation and no residual Unknown row, so the reported checked/Unknown split is not a complete function denominator for such a unit. It promotes nothing today, but it changes the pinned artifacts and the resource selection, so it needs its own parity plan.

named_followups.title: Borrowed pointer-field reads as contracted-call actuals
named_followups.why: premise 5 refuses every pointer field today; without this the constructor call statement is rejected before the declared contract is consulted, and O04 cannot bind its chunk identity.

named_followups.title: Per-arm constructor-to-caller cleanup discharge on the four early-return arms of flb_input_chunk_create
named_followups.why: the single bounded path O00 scoped. Needs C02-P, array-declarator admission, three borrowed callee declarations and per-exit disposition; the success exit, the unenumerated exit and the descriptor/mapping identities stay out of scope.

named_followups.title: Bind non-digest manifest declarations to the executable's embedded template at enable time
named_followups.why: schema-valid, digest-intact edits to limits and targets pass qcorec plugins verify/enable; only package.py verify, which executes the package's self-check, detects them. It cannot admit a Safe verdict, but it changes what the enforced profile installs.

named_followups.title: Represent a source set whose C sources live at the checkout root
named_followups.why: SourceRootSelection admits only Component::Normal segments, so `.` is rejected even where the loader never reads the root. This prevents a sound result rather than an unsound one, and its repair is a PROFILE_MANIFEST_VERSION decision.

named_followups.title: Consume a second real CMake C project's unmodified compile database
named_followups.why: compile_db accepts four frontend flags; Libevent's own CMakeLists appends 18 more unconditionally. Each additional flag needs a preservation argument through preprocessing, syntax and the typed AST.

named_followups.title: Implement the L21.1 reason-code vocabulary for uncovered obligations
named_followups.why: specified prose today with a mapping onto the real strings. Either carrier moves a pinned artifact: DerivationIncomplete is digest-bearing in every evidence-v2 request and witness, and the audit report's per-unit reason is in all four 185-unit artifacts. Environment failures must stay their own category and never be relabelled as source defects.

named_followups.title: Make the CT manifest and its summarizer stage-derived (T00.1-T00.9)
named_followups.why: manifest stage statuses are host-unconditional strings, `cfg` and `type_checker` conflate four real passes, sanitizer evidence is recorded rather than gated, and acceptance.json's two scalars treat a source-rejection case and a four-scenario native case as one identical unit of coverage.

named_followups.title: Composite premise union, per-capability build digests, distinct observation obligation ids, absent-provider dispatch verdict
named_followups.why: four recorded completeness boundaries: the published representative carries one component's coverage/bounds/provenance (conservative), derive_task binds build_digest to the capability's semantic profile (two capabilities of one program always QP015), ObservationCoverageComplete yields one obligation id for two providers (sound only because every component must be Safe, now pinned), and dispatch_scope continues past an unregistered provider so composed.verdict alone can read Safe while verified() is false (masked by Q700).

named_followups.title: Integrate the proposed CT26/CT27/CT29/CT30 mappings through the CT harness
named_followups.why: T03 measured parser/type_checker (and for CT26 reference_execution and native_backend) stages with archived fixtures, but the harness fails closed on a fixture directory whose manifest row reads unmapped, so acceptance needs fixture relocation plus a manifest edit plus a harness run in one deliberate change. CT stays 11/50 until then.

named_followups.why: the reviewed design admits ~9 corpus functions alone and ~25 with C02-P; the emulation probe is measurably more permissive than the designed route at component withdrawal (pinned), and W4 can publish an InferredValidated record derived using a declaration for the same function (U7, observation not defect).

named_followups.title: Remaining confinement bounds: per-execution child quota, default profile wiring, unexecuted refusal grounds in CI
named_followups.why: linux-confined-v1 confines filesystem and network only; no seccomp/cgroup/other namespace, admitted paths stay fully reachable, and refusal grounds 1 (non-Linux) and 4 (kernel without Landlock/userns) are implemented but were not executed on this host - a CI-matrix item.

named_followups.title: Remaining in-process ChunkIO capabilities with named blockers
named_followups.why: thirteen in-process modules stay: list-unlink relates two summaries, the memory-backend destructor carries a call in its path, the cleanup-outcome family carries descriptor/mapping residual custody, traversal/parent_teardown are behind the sealed SourceMatch boundary, and the rest are compositions.

named_followups.title: RLIMIT_NPROC conformance test is load-dependent
named_followups.why: a_declared_process_limit_stops_the_fixture_from_forking installs RLIMIT_NPROC=1, which counts every process of the real UID, so under load the host observes Io(Broken pipe) instead of Terminated. Two independent runs reproduced it; it passes in isolation and passed both merged full-gate runs. The assertion is deliberately not weakened.
